segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [soft harbour water lapping] [softly] Let hearing open like a dark harbour at night. You do not need to identify every vessel; simply notice where each light appears.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find the furthest sound available. Let it blink at the horizon, faint but complete.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Move to a sound in the middle distance. Notice its texture, rhythm, and the silence around it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft fabric rustling] Now hear something close: breath, fabric, a tiny mechanical hum. This is the lamp beside the dock.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose one sound and stay with it for a while. When attention sails away, guide it back by the same small beacon.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let that sound go and choose another. Attention can turn gracefully without declaring the first sound wrong.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice sounds arriving from the left... then the right... ahead... and behind, if those directions are available.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Open to the entire harbour. Loud and quiet sounds share one field, appearing and disappearing by themselves.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] There is no perfect listening state. Even distraction is another brief signal noticed by awareness.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Feel the body in the room and let the harbour remain open as you return to seeing.
